in_text_mentions: Diagnosis of lobomycosis by direct examination of skin smears (Figure 6) enables rapid management of patients, with treatment instituted within a few days of diagnosis. Although histological examination on skin biopsy takes longer to obtain, initial management can be corrected secondarily according to the classification: proposal of adjuvant treatment in the case of a single lesion that has been operated and showing high fungal density and a high risk of recurrence (major form).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Caption attributes panel A to lobomycosis minor form unifocal lesion; image shows nodular keloidal lesion on leg, matching vocabulary. B: Caption attributes panel B to lobomycosis major form unifocal; in-text explicitly calls it atypical macule. Retained as early/infiltrated plaque-type lesion with atypical presentation. C: Caption attributes panel C to lobomycosis major form small multifocal lesions; stacked images show small nodular lesions on ear/face consistent with keloidal nodules. D: Caption attributes panel D to typical major multifocal severe lobomycosis; image shows multiple large keloidal nodular verrucous lesions on arm, leg and trunk.

panels.figure_caption: Clinical aspects of lobomycosis cases in French Guiana. (A) Minor form: unifocal lesion with low fungal density and a complete response. (B) Major form: unifocal but medium-density, clinical relapse. (C) Major form: small but multifocal lesions and high fungal density; clinical relapse after multiple surgeries. (D) Typical major form: multifocal severe and high density, clinical relapse.
in_text_mentions: Most patients had unilobed or multilobed nodular lesions (90%, 28/31), two patients had ulcerated lesions, and one patient had an atypical lesion on the cheek in the form of a centimetric hyperpigmented macule (Figure 1B). Clinical pictures are gathered in Figure 1.

All patients with low fungal density (Hotspot < 400 yeasts per field) had unifocal involvement. Five patients had a low fungal density; all of them had unifocal presentation. Among eight patients with a medium or high density, five had a plurifocal presentations and three had a unifocal one. A low fungal density was associated with a lower risk of multifocal involvement (OR 0.1, 95% CI, [0.01–0.68]; p = 0.044). The only complete response of the cohort was observed in one of these patients (Figure 1A).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real patient clinical photo of 36-year-old with lobomycosis showing solitary shiny erythematous-violaceous nodule on finger, matching keloidal nodules vocabulary. B: Real patient H&E biopsy from same lobomycosis lesion showing giant cells and numerous yeast structures described as typical features of lobomycosis.
panels.attribution_text: Arenas et al. Lobomycosis in Soldiers, Colombia.. Emerging infectious diseases 2019. doi:10.3201/eid2504.181403. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Lobomycosis in a 36-year-old soldier (case-patient 3), Colombia. A) Solitary erythematous-violaceous nodule with a shiny surface and firm consistency (diameter 1 cm) located on the fifth finger of the left hand. B) Hematoxylin and eosin staining of a biopsy specimen from the lesion shows giant cells and numerous yeast structures (original magnification ×20).
in_text_mentions: A 36-year-old soldier reported a 3-year history of a shiny, erythematous, slow-growing, brown nodule with a smooth surface and firm consistency (diameter 1 cm) on the fifth finger of the left hand (Figure 3, panel A). He had no history of trauma and was asymptomatic. A skin biopsy specimen showed typical features of lobomycosis (Figure 3, panel B). Surgical excision was performed, and he was prescribed oral itraconazole (100 mg /d) for 3 months. There was no recurrence of the lesion after a 1-year follow-up.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 7 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G). A: H&E histology panel from lobomycosis case-report article showing narrow-based budding yeasts with sequential budding chains as captioned. B: H&E panel showing narrow-based budding yeasts; caption specifically notes retained tube in 3B&C; yeast chains visible. C: H&E panel explicitly cited for both chain of yeasts and retained tube. D: H&E panel explicitly cited for chain of yeasts. E: H&E panel explicitly cited for chain of yeasts and tube-like isthmus [3E]. F: H&E panel part of same figure showing thick-walled narrow-based budding yeasts; no other disease mentioned. G: H&E panel explicitly cited for multiple irregular non sequential budding [3G] in lobomycosis case.

panels.figure_caption: H & E. [Fig A, x 40; Fig B, C, D, x 100; Fig E, F, G x 200]. Numerous thick walled ‘narrow based’ budding yeasts in a mucoid to necrotic background, many of which show ‘tube like isthmus’ connecting parent cell with daughter cells [3E, short black arrow head]. Many of these yeasts show ‘retained tube’ after the detachment from parent cell [3B&C, short black arrow head]. They also showed characteristic multiple ‘sequential’ budding resulting in ‘chain of yeasts’ [3A, C, D &E, long black arrow heads] and multiple irregular ‘non sequential’ budding [3G, short black arrow head].
in_text_mentions: well as in radiating chains. They showed ‘single’ narrow based budding (Figure 1, Figure 2) as well as ‘multiple’ narrow based budding including ‘sequential budding’ resulting in “chains of yeasts” (Figure 3 and Figure 4) and multiple ‘non sequential budding (Figure 3 and Figure 4). Characteristically, the parent cell and daughter cells were connected by ‘narrow stalk’ or “tube like isthmus” (also called ‘connecting tubes’) (Figure 3 and Figure 4).
